symptom: **Boot-time window flash burst — actual root cause (Windows)**: After exhaustive process-tracking and HWND-event tracking proved the visible "dozens of CMD-like flashes" during startup were **not** subprocess windows, the source was identified as ~150 transient top-level Qt windows titled "OWLLM" being created and shown rapidly.
fix:
Two distinct fixes were required:
1. `LLM/smart_installer.py` was running ~67 `python.exe -c "import <pkg>; print(<pkg>.__version__)"` subprocesses during the requirements-checklist scan (one per package, with `subprocess_flags = {}` after the visibility-first reset). Replaced the 6 inline subprocess loops plus `_verify_import` and the same-Python branch of `_verify_torch` with two new helpers `_probe_module_version` / `_probe_module_importable` that use `importlib.metadata.version()` and `importlib.util.find_spec()` in-process when `check_python == sys.executable`. Foreign-venv probes (install-time only) still fall back to subprocess. Eliminated all ~67 boot-time subprocess flashes; verified by 1ms ToolHelp process tracker.
2. `LLM/desktop_app/model_card_widget.py`: `ModelCard.__init__` and `DownloadedModelCard.__init__` instantiated every internal `QLabel(...)` and `QPushButton(...)` without passing `self` as the parent. Each parentless child briefly became a top-level "OWLLM"-titled HWND when `setVisible(True)` or stylesheet polish ran before the layout chain reached the QFrame. ~12 labels per card × ~12 cards = ~144 transient top-level windows during `_refresh_models`. Fixed by passing `self` as the parent to every `QLabel` / `QPushButton` constructor in the file. Also added explicit `parent=` kwargs at the `ModelCard(...)` / `DownloadedModelCard(...)` / `PackageCard(...)` call sites in `desktop_app/main.py` (`_refresh_models`, `_rebuild_model_card`, search results loop, `_refresh_requirements_grid`). Verified: 152 OWLLM-titled top-level windows reduced to 6 legitimate ones (splash, MainWindow, HybridFrameWindow + Qt internals), confirmed independently by both a `SetWinEventHook` HWND tracker (`LLM/tools/debug_window_tracker.py`) and a Python-level `QWidget.show` / `setVisible` tracer (`LLM/tools/trace_window_creation.py`, activated via `LOCALLLM_TRACE_WIDGETS=1`).
3. `LLM/desktop_app/splash_screen.py` + the `__main__` startup block in `desktop_app/main.py`: removed the per-progress-tick `QApplication.processEvents()` calls that were flushing the entire pending event queue (HWND-creation, show, paint events for every widget the MainWindow was building) at progress-bar phase changes (50%, 90%, 100%). Replaced with synchronous `splash.repaint()` so only the splash itself repaints. The replacement is documented in a comment block at the call site explaining why `processEvents()` must never be reintroduced there.

symptom: **Root-cause fix for CMD window flashes (Windows)**: Added a process-wide subprocess boundary guard at `LLM/core/win_subprocess_guard.py` that patches **every** Windows spawn path the app can reach: `subprocess.Popen.__init__`, `_winapi.CreateProcess`, `os.system`, `os.popen`, and `QProcess` (when the PySide6 API is available).
fix:
All patches force `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` + hidden `STARTUPINFO`, respect explicit `CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE` opt-outs, are idempotent, and degrade to no-ops on non-Windows.
Critically, the guard also **propagates to grandchild Python processes** via `LLM/sitecustomize.py`. Python auto-imports `sitecustomize` from any entry on `sys.path`/`PYTHONPATH` at interpreter startup, so every child Python we spawn (uvicorn, pip, health-check probes, onboarding workers) installs the guard at its own startup — meaning pip's internal compiler spawns and uvicorn's library subprocesses also run without consoles. The guard inserts `LLM/` into `PYTHONPATH` when installed so child processes inherit it transparently.
Installed at: `desktop_app/main.py` (pre-import + re-applied post-PySide6-import), `scripts/llm_server_start.py`, `LAUNCHER.py`, `pip_worker.py`. Diagnostic: set `LOCALLLM_SPAWN_TRACE=1` to log every intercepted spawn to `~/localllm_spawn_trace.log` for pinpointing any remaining flash sources. Set `LOCALLLM_DISABLE_NOWINDOW_GUARD=1` to opt out in child processes.
Note: PySide6 6.8.1 does NOT expose `QProcess.setCreateProcessArgumentsModifier`, so `apply_create_no_window` has historically been a silent no-op; the guard now logs this to the trace file when active. QProcess-spawned console children (training/inference/MCP sites) will only gain full console suppression on PySide6 versions that add the API.

Per-model venv guard propagation (Windows)
Root-cause fix for the "isolate button always flashes" and "restart flashes" regressions that remained after the main `.pth` + `PYTHONPATH` strategy landed.
fix: Each `LLM/.envs/<env_key>/.venv/` has its own isolated `site-packages`, so the main venv's `localllm_guard.pth` was never visible to per-model python.exe — every onboarding/isolate/probe spawned from a per-model venv started *without* the guard, and any grandchild it forked (pip build workers, setup.py compilers, git clones, etc.) produced visible console windows. Fixed by adding `install_guard_into_venv(venv_path)` and `sweep_install_guard_into_envs()` in `core/win_subprocess_guard.py`: both write a tiny `localllm_guard.pth` + `localllm_guard_boot.py` pair into the target venv's site-packages so its interpreter auto-imports the guard at startup. `install_windows_subprocess_guard()` now runs the sweep on main-app startup (covering all pre-existing per-model venvs), and both `core/envs/env_registry.py::_create_env()` and `core/environment_manager.py` install the guard immediately after each successful venv creation (before any pip install, so even first-install compiler spawns are hidden). Verified end-to-end: child python spawned from a per-model venv now logs intercepted spawns to the trace file with `cf=0x8000000` (CREATE_NO_WINDOW) applied.

fix(gpu): kill all auto-pin / PCI override magic; user picks, we pass through
User: 'I HAVE TO BE FREE TO SELECT THE FUCKING GPU I WANT TO USE.'

fix:
Three layers of well-intentioned magic were rewriting
the index between the dropdown and the subprocess:

1. nvidia-smi was used to enumerate GPUs for the dropdown, but
   nvidia-smi's --query-gpu=index returns the legacy
   FASTEST_FIRST default-driver order, NOT the order torch sees.
2. The dropdown then sorted by memory and remapped indices via a
   _orig_index field that _sort_gpus_by_memory unconditionally
   OVERWROTE with the loop position â€” losing the original CUDA
   index. So 'GPU 0: 4090' in the dropdown actually mapped to
   whatever happened to be at position 0 in the sorted list, not
   cuda:0.
3. The GUI then exported CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID alongside the
   chosen index, switching the runtime to a DIFFERENT enumeration
   than the dropdown was built against. Mismatch -> training landed
   on whichever physical GPU the new ordering placed at the picked
   position. On this user's box that was the A2000.

Single source of truth now:

* GUI dropdown is built directly from torch.cuda IN THE WORKLOAD
  VENV â€” same torch that runs finetune.py. We subprocess-call
  python -c 'import torch; emit json' against the venv interpreter
  and use those exact (cuda_idx, name, mem_gb) rows. The dropdown
  shows 'cuda:0 â€” RTX 4090 (22.5 GB)' / 'cuda:1 â€” RTX A2000
  (11.2 GB)'. No nvidia-smi cross-referencing, no _orig_index, no
  memory sorting that loses the CUDA index.

* On click the chosen cuda_idx is exported as CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES
  with NO CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER override. torch in the subprocess uses
  the same default ordering the dropdown was built from, so the
  picked index lands on the picked GPU. Period.

* finetune.py: removed _autoselect_single_gpu_pre_torch() entirely.
  No 'we picked the largest one for you' fallback. If
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES isn't set, torch sees all GPUs and the model
  goes to cuda:0; that's the user's call. Removed the
  CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER mention from the log (it's no longer touched
  anywhere).

Verified: workload venv's torch.cuda reports
  cuda:0 -> RTX 4090, cuda:1 -> RTX A2000

Pick the 4090 -> CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -> torch sees only the 4090
in finetune.py. Pick the A2000 -> CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 -> torch
sees only the A2000.

symptom:
fix(finetune): bf16 load on Ampere+ GPUs (was forcing fp32, hit Win pagefile)
User pushed back on a previous diagnosis: '24 GB VRAM, why is Windows
page file even relevant?' They were right.
fix:
Two compounding things:

1. gemma-4-E4B is 16 GB on disk (fp16-stored). Bigger than the
   'E4B' suffix suggests at first glance â€” it's a 7B-class model.

2. finetune.py's load path forced FP32 whenever bitsandbytes wasn't
   loadable:
       load_kwargs['torch_dtype'] = torch.float32  # 16 GB -> ~32 GB
   On Windows, transformers' safe_open mmaps the file before
   materialising. The OS reserves page-file backing proportional to
   the commit size, and the default page file rejected the 32 GB
   mapping with 'OSError 1455 paging file too small' â€” even on a
   machine with 24 GB VRAM and 64 GB RAM. The real fix is not 'grow
   page file', it's 'don't load fp32 on a 4090'.

Three load tiers now, in preference order:
  1. bitsandbytes 4-bit (if loadable)              â€” ~4 GB
  2. bf16 on Ampere+ GPUs (compute capability >=8) â€” ~14 GB
       full fp32 dynamic range, no GradScaler needed (different
       from fp16's quirks). 4090 / A100 / H100 support this in
       hardware.
  3. fp32 fallback                                 â€” ~28 GB
       last resort for old GPUs or weird configs.

Also added low_cpu_mem_usage=True so weights load lazily into the
device â€” no full state-dict copy in CPU RAM during safe_open's mmap
pass. _should_use_bf16() helper (added earlier in 00ebb86) gates the
tier-2 selection on hardware support.

Net for the user's 4090: gemma-4-E4B loads in ~14 GB instead of
~32 GB. Page-file pressure goes away without touching Windows
config.

   and got dropped. Added 'model' to the assistant-role set; also
   switched to 'first user/first assistant' capture so multi-turn
   datasets don't overwrite as the loop advances.

   amp backend automatically based on fp16/bf16 flags). Removed the

   pin to the biggest one and tell the user. Set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES
   to override (the Train tab UI's GPU selector still works).

symptom:
fix(spawn): sanitise env dict â€” Popen WinError 87 was killing every training run
Caught with the new spawn.log instrumentation:

  Popen FAIL OSError: OSError(22, 'The parameter is incorrect', None, 87, None)
    errno=22 winerror=87
    strerror=The parameter is incorrect

WinError 87 = ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER.
fix:
cmd path was fine, cwd existed,
argv was clean, total cmdline well under 32 KB. So it's the env dict.

Root cause: Windows os.environ inherits cmd.exe's per-drive 'drive
variables' â€” '=C:', '=D:', '=ExitCode', '=ExitCodeAscii' â€” these
start with '=' and are documented Windows behaviour for tracking
per-drive cwd. But Python's subprocess.Popen on Windows rejects ANY
env key starting with '=' and dies with the famously unhelpful
WinError 87, taking the whole training spawn down one millisecond
into the process.

We were inheriting os.environ via qprocess_environment_to_environ()
and passing the inherited dict straight to Popen, dragging the bad
'=' keys with us.

Fix in HiddenSubprocessRunner.start(): one extra pass before Popen
that drops:
  * keys starting with '='     (the actual culprit)
  * non-str keys or values     (Popen requires str)
  * keys or values with '\x00' (Popen rejects)
  * empty keys                 (defensive)
Logs which keys got dropped to spawn.log so any future env-related
spawn failure has a paper trail.

on the user's actual click. With this fix, the equivalent click
should reach Popen with a clean env and the training subprocess
will actually start.

AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained() then treated the argument as

ignoring the local copy at LLM/models/google__gemma-4-E4B-it/ that

  * BEFORE building the finetune cmd, look in LLM/models/<slug>/ for
    a directory containing config.json. If found, pass the ABSOLUTE
    LOCAL PATH to finetune.py instead of the hub id. transformers
    detects local-dir input and skips the network entirely.
  * Two candidate slug forms checked: the dropdown text as-is AND
    the hub-id-with-'/'-replaced-by-'__' form. Covers both folder
    naming conventions in LLM/models/.
  * If no local copy is found (legacy 'user typed a hub id but
    didn't download') the launcher falls back to the hub id with a
    [WARN] line so the user understands why network access is being
    used.

      [INFO] Using local model directory: C:\...\models\google__gemma-4-E4B-it
    â€” visibly confirms transformers is loading from disk.

disk with the right files; the new path resolution will pick that
up. Next training click loads from the SSD, no HF round-trip, no
'where's it downloading what' confusion.

   the LEGACY installer_gui.py (the tkinter window in the screenshot).

   torch-probe failure path. All 'environment needs work' triggers
   now route through the same Qt repair window: missing venv,

Not actually stuck â€” it's the torch trio

buffers ALL of pip's stdout/stderr until the process exits. For pip

- keeps a 400-line ring buffer (~4 KB) so the tail is available for
  inclusion in error messages
- enforces the timeout from inside the read loop instead of relying
  on subprocess.run's blocking timeout (which can't fire while
  Windows pip is mid-download)

the cu121-index trio reinstall paths. The user sees pip's progress
bar live, the percentage tick, the 'Downloading torch-2.5.1...'
lines, etc. â€” instead of a still cursor.

fix(launcher): safe-mode boot when torch stack is broken in the workload venv
OWLLM runs INSIDE the workload venv (LLM/.envs/<env_key>/.venv) â€” the
same venv the in-app repair UI is supposed to fix.

When that venv has
a broken torch stack (torchvision._C.pyd ABI mismatch, CPU-only torch,
missing libtorch DLL) the moment any tab touches torch the whole
process is killed by Windows with no Python traceback. The repair UI
becomes unreachable. Chicken-and-egg.

'import PySide6.QtCore', so a broken torch stack always passed and
the app launched into a venv that was guaranteed to crash on first
torch use.

* check_torch_stack_health(venv_python) â€” subprocess-runs
  'import torch, torchvision, torchaudio' and matches the failure
  text against the same ABI-mismatch fingerprints
  immutable_installer._ensure_torch_trio_coherent uses
  (intrusive_ptr_target, c10::, _C.pyd, 'could not be located in the
  dynamic link library', 'undefined symbol', etc). ~1 s when healthy.

* launch_safe_mode_installer(reason) â€” when the probe fails, spawn
  installer_gui.py with the BUNDLED LLM/python_runtime/pythonX.Y/
  python.exe â€” NOT the broken workload venv. The installer GUI only
  needs tkinter + stdlib subprocess to drive InstallerV2, so the
  bootstrap runtime can run it standalone. This honours the
  self-contained design intent (no system Python needed) AND breaks
  the chicken-and-egg.

and the dependency check. If the probe trips: route to safe mode and
exit; do NOT proceed to launch_app.

fix(repair): pip 26+ progress-bar flag + torch trio ABI coherence
THE REAL BLOCKER (revealed by 44a6c83's error capture):

  option --progress-bar: invalid choice: 'ascii'
    (choose from 'auto', 'on', 'off', 'raw')

User's pip is 26.1.

pip 24+ removed the 'ascii' progress-bar choice.
Every wheelhouse download was failing on this one CLI flag, and the
empty-stderr bug we shipped 44a6c83 to fix was hiding it. With pip
download dead, the repair fell through to a direct-PyPI path that
installed torch and torchvision out-of-sync, which is what
triggered the Windows pop-up:

  could not be located in the dynamic link library .../torchvision/_C.pyd

   We don't need pip's own widget â€” we parse percent/size from its

   _ensure_torch_trio_coherent step that runs before VerificationSystem.

   matches the failure against ABI-mismatch fingerprints (intrusive_ptr,
   c10::, _C.pyd, 'could not be located in the dynamic link library',
   'undefined symbol'). On a hit, uninstalls + force-reinstalls the

   wheels), PyTorch CUDA index as fallback. Cheap when already coherent

symptom:
fix(wheelhouse): surface pip's real error instead of an empty string
THIS is why every repair failure has been impossible to diagnose:
_download_wheel was throwing away pip's stderr.
fix:
The streaming reader
split stderr by carriage returns into 'parts', kept only parts[-1]
(the tail) for the next chunk, ran the inner parts[:-1] through a
progress-bar regex, and then DROPPED them on the floor. When pip
emitted real error text at the end of a failed run, those lines
went through the progress regex (which didn't match), and were
discarded.

The user-facing message:
    'Failed to download critical package safetensors: '
                                                       ^^^^
                                                  empty error string

Fix: keep TWO buffers in the read loop. stderr_buf stays as the
carriage-return tail used to update the live progress bar. A new
stderr_all_lines accumulator collects every non-progress line â€”
that's what gets returned when pip fails, so the dialog now shows
'No matching distribution found for safetensors>=0.4.5,<1.0' or
'HTTPError 503' or 'SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED' or whatever the
actual blocker is.

Bumped the truncation cap from 500 to 2000 chars so multi-line pip
error blocks (the version list pip helpfully prints under 'No
matching distribution found') survive.

symptom:
fix(window): all 8 edges resizable via WM_NCHITTEST, not just two
The MainWindow is frameless (no native title bar) and was relying on
its own mousePressEvent / mouseMoveEvent to detect edge drags.
fix:
That
path only fires when no child widget eats the mouse â€” which means
resizing was effectively dead on every edge that overlapped a tab
bar, button, scroll area, or any custom widget. So users could only
drag the few uncluttered edges and the rest looked broken.

Override nativeEvent on Windows to handle WM_NCHITTEST. We map the
8 hit zones to the standard HT* codes (HTLEFT/HTRIGHT/HTTOP/HTBOTTOM
plus the 4 corners) and let the OS drive the resize loop. Windows'
own non-client hit-testing happens before any Qt widget sees the
click, so resizing now works regardless of what's under the cursor.
Maximised / fullscreen are skipped so the window doesn't try to
resize from inside the screen edge.

The Qt-level resize fallback in mousePress/mouseMoveEvent stays in
place untouched â€” non-Windows builds and the HybridFrameWindow Tool
overlay still rely on it.

symptom:
fix(installer): heal python-tag mismatch by re-downloading wheels, NOT rebuilding venv
Previous attempt at the python-tag self-heal tried to destroy the
existing venv and recreate it with a matching bundled Python.
fix:
That
plan is fundamentally broken on Windows: OWLLM is RUNNING from the
venv it would need to delete, so python.exe and every loaded .pyd
(charset_normalizer/md.cp311-win_amd64.pyd in the user's case) are
locked. WinError 5 every time.

Worse, the bundled python_runtime/python3.12 is the EMBEDDABLE
distribution â€” no Lib/venv module â€” so the fallback branch
re-grabbed sys.executable, which IS the locked venv's python.exe.
The "fix" tried to operate on the very interpreter executing it.

New approach: leave the venv alone. When the cpXY tag stamped into
the wheelhouse wheels doesn't match the venv's Python, refresh the
wheelhouse for the venv's tag instead. The venv is the deployment
target and the source of truth for the Python version; the
wheelhouse is just a cache.

  1. Probe the venv's cpXY tag (e.g. cp311) and parse the
     wheelhouse's tag from the first .whl filename (e.g. cp312).
  2. On mismatch, parse the venv tag back to (3, 11) and call
     WheelhouseManager.prepare_wheelhouse(cuda_config, (3,11),
     force_redownload=True). This redownloads wheels matching the
     venv. Zero file-lock risk because the venv tree isn't touched.
  3. PHASE 4 then finds the right wheels and installs them.

If the wheelhouse refresh itself fails, surface a clean message
naming the situation instead of letting pip's cryptic "no matching
distribution" mask the real reason.

fix(installer): self-heal python-tag mismatch between venv and wheelhouse
Symptom:
  [1/38] Installing torch...
fix:
âœ— Could not find a version that satisfies torch==2.5.1+cu121
    (from versions: none)
  ERROR: No matching distribution found for torch==2.5.1+cu121

Root cause: the wheelhouse held cp312 wheels
(torch-2.5.1+cu121-cp312-cp312-win_amd64.whl â€¦) but the existing
venv was Python 3.11.9. pip refuses every wheel because the cpXY
platform tag doesn't match the venv's interpreter, even though
``--no-index --find-links`` correctly points at the wheelhouse.
The user's screen reads "Installation failed" with nothing the
user can click to actually fix it â€” that's the opposite of the
"self-healing, self-contained, self-installed" promise.

Fix: on the resume branch (existing venv detected), probe the
venv's cpXY tag and compare against the cp tag stamped into the
first ``.whl`` filename in the wheelhouse. If they don't match:

  1. Find a python_runtime/pythonX.Y bundled folder that produces
     the required cp tag (we ship 3.11 and 3.12).
  2. Switch self.python_executable to that runtime.
  3. Tear down the wrong-version venv and rebuild â€” every wheel is
     incompatible anyway, so there's nothing worth saving.
  4. Force skip_installed=False so PHASE 4 installs every required
     package against the freshly-rebuilt venv.

Two new helpers carry the logic: _check_python_tag_compat returns
(compatible, venv_tag, required_tag); _find_bundled_python_for_tag
maps "cp312" back to a python.exe under python_runtime/python3.12/.

If no matching bundled runtime exists we surface a clear error
naming the missing version instead of letting pip's "no matching
distribution" mask the real reason.

symptom:
fix(canvas): repulsion now acts on the curve LINE, not just control points
Previous pass nudged each control point away from obstacle CENTRES
once.
fix:
That mostly worked but the bezier curve is not its control
points â€” the puppet-strings can sit far from a box while the
actual line still grazes the corner.

Now we iteratively relax the control points so the SAMPLED CURVE
stays clear:

  1. Sample the cubic at fixed t-values (16 samples).
  2. For each sample compute net repulsion from every obstacle's
     RECT (distance to the closest point on the rect, not centre â†’
     handles long boxes correctly). Force is strong if the sample
     is inside a box, decays linearly to zero at REPEL_RANGE
     outside.
  3. Back-propagate each sample's force to c1 and c2 weighted by
     the cubic Bernstein basis at that t (which is exactly each
     control point's influence on the curve at t).
  4. Apply with damping; repeat for REPEL_ITERS iterations.

Result: the visible LINE keeps its distance from every box that
isn't its own endpoint. Multiple obstacles' forces sum, so an
arrow squeezed between two boxes routes through the middle of the
gap instead of grazing whichever box happens to be nearer.

The rect-distance + inside-box centre-push handling means a
sample that would otherwise overlap a box gets shoved out
deterministically.

Symptom: GLM 4.7 (and any other locally-onboarded model with more

dropdown despite there only being one weights file on disk and only
one server able to run.
fix:
Root cause: list_entries returned one ModelEntry per row from
list_ready_models(). When the user re-onboarded a model under a
different model_id (e.g. user-typed slug vs canonical id, or two
HF repo variants of the same gguf), each onboarding row became its
own dropdown entry â€” but they all resolve to the same .gguf path
and so are functionally indistinguishable.

Fix: bucket READY rows by absolute resolved base_model_path. Within
each bucket, keep one representative, preferring the row that's
currently RUNNING, then the row whose model_id matches its
canonical_id (the authoritative name), then insertion order. Rows
without a base_model_path are kept as-is so we never hide unrelated
models we just can't compare.

fix(server): real token-level streaming for chat completions
Previously /v1/chat/completions ran model.generate() to completion
before the streaming branch even started, then chopped the finished
string into 64-char SSE chunks.
fix:
With Cline-style 12k-token prompts
that's several minutes of total silence â€” Cline's UI gives up before
the first byte arrives. The model wasn't slow OR stuck, it was just
holding everything until done and never streaming a real token.

Added run_adapter_backend.generate_text_streaming(): a generator that
uses transformers.TextIteratorStreamer plus a background generate()
thread for the transformers path, and llama-cpp-python's native
stream=True iterator for the GGUF path. Falls back to the
non-streaming function on any failure or older transformers.

server_app.chat_completions now branches: when stream=True AND the
backend supports per-token streaming (transformers / llama-cpp), the
SSE iterator pulls from generate_text_streaming and yields each token
as it arrives. Multimodal and ExLlamaV2 stay on the existing
generate-then-chunk path because their backends don't expose
token-level streaming yet.

Net effect for Cline / Continue / Open WebUI: tokens render as the
model produces them; clients no longer time out waiting for a single
big response.

symptom:
fix(shutdown): kill ALL descendant processes on app close, not just uvicorn
closeEvent's cleanup was missing several worker-process classes:
- Python in-process model loaders (run_adapter_backend, llama-cpp-python,
  etc.) â€” the WMI filter only matched server_app / bundled_proxy_server.
fix:
- Native llama-server.exe workers spawned by bundled_proxy_server â€” not a
  Python process at all, so every python.exe filter missed them. These
  are the actual GPU-VRAM holders.
- Anything else spawned indirectly via "model_server" / "inference_worker"
  / "owllm-server" entry points.

1. Widened the python.exe WMI filter to also catch run_adapter_backend,
   llama_cpp, and the broader OWLLM worker naming patterns.
2. taskkill /F /IM llama-server.exe /T â€” wipes any native llama-server
   binary the bundled proxy spawned.

   orphan children of children get cleaned up regardless of executable
   name. Excludes the app's own PID so it doesn't kill itself before
   finishing the rest of closeEvent.

kills, so a graceful shutdown still gets first crack â€” this is purely a
fallback for processes the graceful path missed.

symptom:
fix(gpu,cline): auto-offload to NVIDIA GPU + stream SSE chunks unbuffered
The bundled llama-server and the run_adapter_backend GGUF path both
defaulted to CPU unless the launcher explicitly set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES.
fix:
On a normal Windows install with an NVIDIA card the launcher doesn't set
it, so models silently loaded into RAM, ran at CPU speed, and Cline timed
out before the first token. Both paths now probe for a usable NVIDIA GPU
via nvidia-smi (and torch.cuda.is_available as a backup) and full-offload
when one is found, unless CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES or LLM_*_N_GPU_LAYERS

backends can take tens of seconds and kills token-by-token streaming.
Switched to resp.read1(4096) so each SSE event from llama-server flushes
to Cline as soon as it arrives, even when the model is on CPU.

  the home page writes UUIDs alongside indices and migrates legacy configs

handler now reads live checkbox state instead of the on-disk config (which
could be stale during a hot patch), and the warning only fires when

Root-cause for 'isolate button flashes' and 'flash on restart after close'
regressions that persisted after the main .pth + PYTHONPATH strategy:
each LLM/.envs/<env_key>/.venv has its own isolated site-packages, so the
main venv's localllm_guard.pth was never visible to per-model python.exe.
fix:
Every onboarding/isolate/probe spawned from a per-model venv started
WITHOUT the guard and any grandchild it forked (pip build workers,

  and sweep_install_guard_into_envs() helpers. They drop a tiny
  localllm_guard.pth + localllm_guard_boot.py pair into the target
  venv's site-packages so its interpreter auto-imports the guard at
  startup. Boot module is generated with the absolute LLM root baked
  in so it works without PYTHONPATH being set. install_windows_subprocess_guard()
  now runs the envs sweep automatically at the end of setup.
- core/envs/env_registry.py: install guard into freshly-created venv
  BEFORE any pip install runs, so even first-install compiler spawns
  are hidden.

  paths in this legacy environment manager.
- CHANGELOG.md: describe root-cause and end-to-end verification.

intercepted subprocess.Popen / _winapi.CreateProcess with cf=0x8000000
(CREATE_NO_WINDOW) applied â€” sweep installed the guard into 20 existing
per-model venvs in this repo and each one now auto-loads it.

symptom:
Fix Install Dependencies button to work correctly
ROOT CAUSE:
- requirements.txt had 'torch>=2.0.0' which pip installs as latest CPU version (2.9.1+cpu)
- Install Dependencies button only ran install_dependencies(), not full smart installer
- Result: Wrong PyTorch version, wrong build (CPU instead of CUDA)

1.
fix:
Removed torch from requirements.txt
   - SmartInstaller handles PyTorch with correct CUDA version
   - requirements.txt only has deps that dont need special handling

2. Changed Install Dependencies button to run FULL smart installer
   - Now calls InstallerThread('all') instead of 'dependencies'
   - Runs: PyTorch (correct CUDA) + all dependencies
   - Updated dialog to show what will be installed

3. SmartInstaller.install() now ALWAYS reinstalls PyTorch
   - Forces uninstall + reinstall even if PyTorch found
   - Ensures correct version (2.5.1) and CUDA build (cu118/cu121/cu124)
   - No longer skips if old version detected

Now clicking Install Dependencies will:
- Uninstall wrong PyTorch (2.9.1+cpu)
- Install correct PyTorch (2.5.1+cu118 for T1000)
- Install all dependencies (unsloth, transformers, etc.)
- Everything compatible and working
